title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Innovation and Practice of Digital Technology in Higher Vocational Fashion Courses
description: Review of CLO Academic Month 2024! A conversation with Teacher Zhu Na from Guangdong Technical College, who introduced the college's experience in digital reform in the fashion major, including the daily teaching of CLO, finished product effect presentation, school-industry-enterprise collaborative projects, as well as the impact of the digital museum and virtual simulation system on teaching.
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am very happy to be here today to learn and share with you the application of CLO 3D technology in clothing courses.  
Yesterday, I listened to the sharing of Mr. Gao and Mr. Luo. In fact, I feel that I have gained a lot because I usually take a course on clothing structure.  
From Mr. Gao's sharing of 3D virtual technology and clothing structure courses, I really learned a lot and was deeply inspired. Maybe we will continue to improve in the future.  

Next, I would like to talk about the innovation and practice of our school in digital technology in professional courses.  
In the latest McKinsey report, it was pointed out that in 2030, 800 million people will be replaced by machines. China will face the transformation of professions. From this point of view, our country will face the largest-scale change in employment.  
As a professional education worker, we must always pay attention to the new trends of industry development so that our education can keep up with the pace of the times.  

Next, I will mainly talk about the application of digital technology in our school's clothing professional teaching process. The first is professional accuracy.  
Professional accuracy is important for the development of the industry. In 2035, the key core technologies, especially digitalization, networking, and intelligent development, will have made breakthroughs.  
The clothing industry has made new breakthroughs in new industries, new models, and new services such as design, plating, customization, etc.  
The appearance of ODM, product innovation has created a new model of a soft and fast-reaction supply chain.  
Digital technology and the deep integration of industries, the new industry state, sharing and manufacturing factories will become the standard services of industrial workers.  

Therefore, we have conducted some corporate research and teaching activities many times. We have also made a lot of thoughts and improvements in the application of digital technology in the course.  

In Guangdong province, our school is located in Guangdong province. Guangdong province is a major clothing industry base. The development of the clothing industry is also very rapid. There is a lack of intelligent and information-based talent promotion for corporate transformation and upgrade. New technology and manufacturing integration is a new model for the future. There are still many hard workers in Guangdong province.  

If you think about it, some management people who design and develop projects every year will need to recruit at least 8,000 new people. In Guangdong province, there are about 7 clothing-related vocational schools, about 33 high-quality vocational schools, and about 400 graduates per year in high-quality vocational schools. There will be slightly more in other high-quality vocational schools. On average, there may be about 100 students in each school. There are also some clothing graduates from various places. If this is added up, it will not meet the entire needs of the industry.  

Therefore, we still have a challenging area. There is a lack of talent. There is also a lack of talent in digitalization technology.  

Next, I will talk about the basic situation of our school. There are three majors in our school's clothing academy.  
One is the clothing design and supply industry major. The other is the clothing and clothing industry major. There is also a leather design major.  

There are three directions in the clothing design and supply industry major: engineering, marketing, and needlework.  
One of the biggest characteristics of our school is that there are many people in the clothing industry. Our school is only in the third grade of high school, but the total number of students in our school can reach 3,000. That is to say, there are more than 1,000 graduates per year. It is the largest clothing industry school in South China (Huanan).  

It has 33 clothing design senior engineers. It is a brand demonstration major and a key focus major in Guangdong Province. In general, the school's employment situation has been good in recent years. This is our employment statistics from May 2023. Because we have a relatively large number of graduates—about 1,000 graduates per year—last year there were 1,006 graduates. In May of last year, the employment rate of graduates reached 99.3%.  

Of course, some of our students chose to study in special courses and continued their education in school. Most of the students went to work, but we have about 90% employment of the total number of graduates.  

In order to provide high-quality employment for our students, the teachers in our school actively learn new techniques and methods to improve the quality of clothing education and to optimize the development of the industry.  

In the course of practical education, teachers are also actively developing and using digital resources.  

The second thing I want to talk about is the construction of digital rich energy creation resources.  

First of all, the rise of virtual imaging technology. It can quickly measure fabric, design and modify, implement and present, and smoothly complete transitions between 3D and 2D printing. In addition, it can carry out some diversified array display designs, such as virtual embroidery, and so on.  

The digital technology of clothing allows us to go from digital platform to style design, to virtual clothing production, then audit and modify, and finally connect to smart production. In this way, our design to smart production is fully digitalized.  

Clothing technology is an integral part of our business. Clothing 3D technology can complete the entire process of clothing from construction to implementation through a computer. It can greatly reduce the error rate of paper samples by changing the thinking from 2D to 3D. It can determine the design sample and reduce costs for a green environment.  

For designers, the transition from 2D to 3D is more familiar, and communication with 3D printers is smoother. The design is more reasonable. Clothing 3D technology combines the work of designers, 3D printers, and sample workers, reducing the chance of error.  

Similarly, 3D virtual technology has been used by many companies to achieve cloud-based fashion through virtual fashion. For example, China International Fashion Week is a new ecosystem where virtual fashion shows, virtual clothing shows, and physical-virtual synchronized marketing have been transformed into one.  

Our school is also based on the principle of technology integration, time-lapse integration, and teaching innovation. We have built four centers: the Professional Virtual Fashion Training Center, the Public Virtual Fashion Training Center, the Virtual Fashion Experience Center, and the Virtual Fashion Creative Center.  

In the Professional Special Fashion Training Center, we have the Special Fashion Fashion Center for the fashion industry. Next, we will introduce some resources for cooperation development and application and teaching of virtual fashion. Let me introduce them to you.  

The first one is a virtual certification system designed for the fashion industry. It can help our students participate in some practical fashion shows. Because we have the exam of the 1 plus X certificate for the fashion show, through this practice, we can keep the certificate pass rate relatively high.  

The second one is the virtual certification system for the fashion static exhibition and show. This can combine some design skills and some virtual shows. This is one of the national virtual certification projects. One of the sub-projects is a certification resource for the fashion museum. After we build this resource, we will think about the following courses and will combine them with it. We have already used it for a while.  

There are clothes of various ethnic groups and the clothes of two common ethnic groups in the South China Sea region and the clothes of Lingnan. We also have a museum in the South China Sea region. For example, we can do some project teaching with the class of fashion history and the classes of women's fashion and men's fashion.  

In the fashion history class, there will be various fashion trends. We will guide our students to do some digital restoration. We will put some excellent works into this museum. It is also for the students to do some study. These are some works of our students. Although they are not perfect and still have some shortcomings, I think that through this method, the learning activity of students will be higher.  

After I come out, this is a video I recorded in advance. Let me introduce it to you a little bit. In addition, we have two more ethnic clothes. These two ethnic clothes are Yao and Zhuang. In this video, I will show you the characteristics of Yao and Zhuang ethnic clothes and some of their digital costumes. We have put them all in this video.  

When our students in the design class are in the third year of high school, there is a graduation ceremony. Before they go out, we will have them do a study in advance. In this way, when they are in the ceremony, they will have more goals. These are some of the works of Yao and Zhuang ethnic clothes.  

Finally, we have Lingnan ethnic clothes. In the Lingnan ethnic clothes, we mainly put some of our local, for example, Xiangyunsha, Yuexiu, and some local characteristics of our local clothes. One of them is the clothes of our school, by Chen Yiran. These are some of the products of our collaboration with the school. We will put them in this video. We will also include some of our students' excellent design works and some of their award-winning works in this video.  

This is a brief introduction of our museum. In the following courses, we will still use our resources to let our students learn professional knowledge better.  

Next, we will talk about our school's development and cooperation with the school for virtual design. This is our first virtual project; you will have an understanding of the equipment in advance.  

In terms of design, we have modularized all the parts of the shirt and suit. Students can design the style they want to do in advance through the selection method and then take it to the next course. This is our group outfit. Compared to the previous group outfit, it has one more module. We will put the process of craftsmanship into it. The process of craftsmanship will be more detailed. Students will know how to make it before making it. In this way, they will be able to complete it quickly when they do the actual work.  

Because our high-level vocational schools pay more attention to the training of students' skills, this is the application development of some of the digital resources of our school.  

Next, I will talk about the application in our teaching process. We also carry out some professional reforms in the teaching process. This is in line with the development of our entire industry.  

In terms of professional reform, we include the reform of the talent training model and the reform of the course standards. We also include the requirement of digitalization. We also have the construction of a digital training room and a platform, as I mentioned above.  

In terms of reforming content, we include practical teaching, course improvement and professional improvement, the collaboration of faculty and school, as well as improving our teaching methods, and so on.  

The second is a school-level association. In terms of teaching at the school, we will carry out some digitalization of the school. This includes the education of some system-based digitalized related software, including learning our CLO 3D modeling design software and some design processing software, and we use some cooperative platforms. We will also include some related knowledge in marketing courses.  

The second one is enterprise production. This mainly relies on the collaboration of some school-level partnerships. We carry out high-quality professional planning, and it is very interesting, such as research and development of artificial intelligence technology, research and development of technical patents, and development of our experimental and practical training system, etc.  

In terms of talent employment, we mainly focus on the training of digitalized talents and employment guidance. Here, we have provided guidance on the training of digitalized talents, professional certification, and internship employment, etc.  

We have also established some industrial universities. Here, I have listed two typical ones. One is the Ida Industrial University, which is co-founded by our local Ida Group and Spring Small Technology Co., Ltd., which has established the Spring Small Technology Specialization Institute. This is mainly for the development of some digitalized talents, training, and the exchange of employment teams. The Specialization Institute is mainly digitalized in the field of smart manufacturing.  

Next, these are some projects of our corporate cooperation. This is a project that we led students to participate in last year. This project consists of three series of costumes. The modeling and embroidery videos are all made by our students. This is a small piece of the final film.  

Of course, we cannot produce this scene now. We may also lead students to learn how to build some simple scenes with some third-party software. These are also some corporate cooperation projects that we have completed.  

Next, I would like to talk about some exploratory applications of our teaching methods. We mainly use this virtual imaging technology to adopt modeling, construction, and division tasks to carry out some teaching scenarios for clothing training.  

As shown in this picture, this is a digitalized module in our women's clothing integration course. Here, our students will carry out a 3D digital design at the beginning of the design. Then, after the payment is made, they will go into production.  

Also, in this 3D digital design course, we will introduce real tasks to use the virtual factory to identify equipment, process preparation, and material preparation scenarios to bridge the gap between school and industry.  

This is our 3D, that is, our CLO 3D course. Our school calls it 3D Clothing Design and Application. This course, because we are in the senior stage, is a three-year course. Our professional class time is relatively tight.  

At first, our class was set to 28 students. Later, it was changed to 32 students. Now, if we are students in the engineering class, we may gradually want to add 48 students. It's like this. Because the class time is relatively short, we can only learn some basic content.  

Here are some of our students' works. We also require students to join their own design in the class and then combine it with some of the basics that our teachers have explained. Basically, the works that our students have produced are basically the same, but each of them has different styles and appearances.  

In the initial class, we mainly talked about a T-shirt, shirt, sweater, pants, shirt, and a half-sleeved skirt. It's probably like this. There are some of these craft skills in the back. Many of them are learned by the students themselves after class.  

For example, in the class, there are some things that our teachers can't cover face-to-face. I would recommend our students study in the official class on Bilibili (B station). For example, the last picture in the back is a student's homework. For example, this is a production of a special school, Dengguang. My class teacher didn't talk about it. This student went to study by himself. Of course, if he or she encounters any problems in the learning process, he or she can also communicate with the teacher at any time.  

Next, this is a class on the structure of men's flat surface. In many cases, when we learn this class, our 3D software is actually not learned. So, at this time, our 3D software is actually operated by the teacher when it is in use.  

In addition to CLO 3D, we also use other tools in this class. For example, this is a 3D intelligent measurement mirror. This device can measure size by standing on it and scanning a circle through this mirror. It is not the same as traditional methods. The data may be a little different, but I think it is sufficient for our work.  

The second one is a digital fabric scanner. We scan the fabric in advance here. It is also used for students in CLO 3D to use texture and line drawing. In this way, after the students finish the pattern, they can add the fabric directly and then see the effect.  

These are the three software programs that we use in class.  

In the course of teaching, the application of CLO 3D software is mainly like this. I have two examples here.  

The first one is that when we talk about specification design, we have to explain to the students how many sizes should be added and why these sizes should be added. For example, I used the hard disk in the 3D software here to see what the pressure is like. Then, we can analyze it.  

The second example is that when making shirts, some people may have a demand for uniformity of the shirt. For example, if we want to add the placket. In the traditional way of teaching, we will be taken to the platform to teach. This is very laborious. Now, after we have this software, it is more convenient. We don't have to run around with the platform.  

This is our financial course. The financial course is also prepared by our teacher in advance. We will use 3D to make the financial work in advance. In this way, it is more intuitive than photos.  

This is the e-commerce course. Because there are some photos in the e-commerce course, some students will use 3D software to directly do the work. In fact, the effect may be better than traditional 3D software.  

This is also a project in our women's fashion course. It is a combination of traditional culture and embroidery with some students' works.  

The last thing I want to talk about is graduation design. Here, for graduation design, our school has about 1,000 graduates every year, so not every student has to do a graduation thesis. Some students are in the orderly class. For the students in the orderly class, we don't require them to complete the final task. We require them to adapt the digital 3D clothing to their graduation design.  

This is the work of a student in the orderly class. He made three sets, including accessories for graduation design and the work for graduation design. He made six sets in total. Finally, he made an exhibition. The exhibition here is also because students may not like the 3D software of the scene. In the end, the scene is more flat.  

This is the work of a student in the orderly class. In the beginning, he made the 3D clothing first. This is a photo of the graduation exhibition. The 3D work is displayed at the top. The next is the final result of the 3D work.  

The 3D work is the final result of the 3D work. The 3D work is the final result of the final result. The 3D work is a 3D work of the student.  

This is the final result of the competition of the second year of the 3D work and the international student engineering training in China. This is a work of the first national 3D competition. This student's work won first place in the first prize. It's mainly in terms of design. Another student won the first prize in design.  

This is a prize from another teacher who led a student to participate in a national innovation competition. She also won an award for cooperating with an enterprise.  

What I want to say is that every year, we have a teaching competition in a professional school. Our school won the first prize in the national competition for two consecutive years. In the second year, we won the first prize. In the third year, we won the second prize. In these two competitions, we applied digital technology to the course.  

The first one is a project in the design of women's clothing. We applied the 3D design of women's clothing in the design phase. The second competition was a class in men's clothing craftsmanship. But in the development phase of women's clothing, we also applied the 3D design of women's clothing.  

The last one is a QR code in the virtual interview room of our school. If you are interested, please take a look at the QR code.  

Finally, I will use eight words to explain my sharing. I hope this kind of technology will be born in the future. I hope our professional education work will be better and better.  

Thank you, everyone. That's all for my sharing.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Innovation and Practice of Digital Technology in Higher Vocational Fashion Courses
chunks.content: # Innovation and Practice of Digital Technology in Higher Vocational Fashion Courses This document details the application and integration of digital technology, particularly CLO 3D and virtual imaging, in higher vocational fashion education. It covers industry trends, educational reforms, digital resources, teaching methods, and student achievements, emphasizing the role of digitalization in modernizing fashion curriculum and talent cultivation. --- ## Industry Trends and Educational Context This section outlines the broader industry transformation driven by digital technology, the challenges faced by the fashion industry in Guangdong province, and the imperative for vocational education to adapt to technological advances. - According to McKinsey (latest report), by 2030, approximately 800 million jobs worldwide will be replaced by machines, indicating massive employment shifts in China and globally. - Digitalization, networking, and intelligent development are expected to achieve breakthroughs by 2035, impacting design, plating, customization, ODM (Original Design Manufacturing), and supply chain models. - Guangdong province is a major clothing industry hub undergoing rapid development but faces a shortage of intelligent and information-based talents to aid corporate transformation and upgrade. - Industry demand: Annually, approximately 8,000 new recruits are needed in clothing-related management and design roles in Guangdong. - Supply: There are about 7 clothing-related vocational schools and 33 high-quality vocational schools in Guangdong, graduating roughly 400-500 students annually, which does not meet the industry's talent demand. - Significant gaps exist in talent quantity and digital technology expertise. --- ## Overview of the School and Academic Programs This section introduces the school's structure, majors, student population, faculty expertise, and employment outcomes, highlighting the scale and quality of its vocational fashion education. - The school is located in Guangdong province and is the largest clothing industry vocational school in South China (Huanan) with approximately 3,000 students and over 1,000 graduates yearly. - Three majors within the clothing academy: - Clothing Design and Supply Industry Major (with three directions: engineering, marketing, needlework) - Clothing and Clothing Industry Major - Leather Design Major - Faculty includes 33 senior clothing design engineers. - Recognized as a brand demonstration and key focus major in Guangdong Province. - Employment rate as of May 2023 reached 99.3% among 1,006 graduates. - Approximately 90% of graduates gain employment, with some continuing education. - Teachers actively update skills and incorporate digital resources to improve education quality. --- ## Digital Resource Construction and Virtual Fashion Centers This section covers the establishment of digital infrastructure and virtual fashion centers aimed at integrating technology into fashion education and practice. - Four centers established: - Professional Virtual Fashion Training Center - Public Virtual Fashion Training Center - Virtual Fashion Experience Center - Virtual Fashion Creative Center - Virtual imaging technology capabilities: - Fabric measurement, design modification, 3D-2D transitions, virtual embroidery. - Digital workflow from style design to virtual production, auditing, and smart manufacturing. - CLO 3D technology enables digital construction and implementation of clothing, reducing paper sample errors and costs, and facilitating green production.

Fabric measurement, design modification, 3D-2D transitions, virtual embroidery. - Digital workflow from style design to virtual production, auditing, and smart manufacturing. - CLO 3D technology enables digital construction and implementation of clothing, reducing paper sample errors and costs, and facilitating green production. - Virtual fashion is integrated into large-scale events, e.g., China International Fashion Week, combining virtual fashion shows and synchronized physical-virtual marketing. - Virtual certification systems: - For fashion shows, supporting the 1 plus X certificate exam with high pass rates. - For fashion static exhibitions and museum projects, including ethnic clothing collections from South China Sea and Lingnan regions. - Museums used as teaching aids for digital restoration and historical fashion studies, engaging students in practical projects. - Digital exhibits include ethnic costumes of Yao, Zhuang, and Lingnan, alongside student award-winning designs. --- ## Digital Design and Modular Clothing Projects This section describes modular design methodologies, digital teaching resources, and the integration of craftsmanship processes into virtual design workflows. - Modularization of shirt and suit components allows students to pre-design styles digitally before physical production. - Additional modules added to group outfit projects include detailed craftsmanship processes to enhance students' understanding and production efficiency. - Emphasis on skill training aligns with vocational education priorities. - Digital resource development supports advanced and practical learning. --- ## Teaching Process Reforms and Digitalization This section explains reforms in talent training models, course standards, digital infrastructure, and collaborative platforms to align education with industry needs. - Reforms include: - Talent training model updates - Course standard revisions incorporating digitalization - Construction of digital training rooms and platforms - Enhancement of practical teaching and faculty collaboration - School-wide digital initiatives: - Training in CLO 3D modeling and other design software - Integration of digital knowledge in marketing courses - Enterprise collaboration supports: - AI technology R&D - Technical patent development - Experimental and practical training systems - Talent employment efforts focus on digital skills training, professional certification, and internship guidance. - Industrial-University partnerships: - Example: Ida Industrial University co-founded with Ida Group and Spring Small Technology Co., Ltd., focusing on smart manufacturing digital talents. --- ## Corporate Collaboration and Student Project Involvement This section details student participation in industry projects and the usage of third-party software for scene building and design. - Students led projects involving costume series with modeling and embroidery videos. - Exposure to third-party software for simple scene construction, complementing CLO 3D skills. - Completed corporate cooperation projects demonstrate practical application and industry relevance.
